items.stem: In the Divio documentation system, how does a tutorial differ from a how-to guide?

options.text: A tutorial teaches a beginner through a guided lesson; a how-to solves a specific task for someone who already knows the basics
options.rationale: Correct: they serve different readers and goals.

options.text: A tutorial is reference material listing every parameter
options.rationale: That describes reference, not a tutorial.

options.text: A how-to explains underlying concepts and theory
options.rationale: That describes explanation, not a how-to.

options.text: They are interchangeable names for the same thing

items.stem: Why should a quickstart's example be copy-pasteable and verified?

options.text: A reader can succeed immediately, building trust and reducing support load

options.text: It makes the docs site load faster
It replaces the need for reference docs
options.rationale: Reference is still needed for details.

options.text: It guarantees the library has no bugs

items.stem: Which practices keep documentation trustworthy over time? (Select TWO)

options.text: Treat docs as code and update them in the same pull request as the change
options.rationale: Correct: coupling docs to changes prevents drift.

options.text: Provide minimal, runnable examples that are tested
Write docs once and never revisit them
Fill reference pages with marketing language
options.rationale: False; reference should be precise and factual.
